findings.text: Early console probe for the debug communication channel spins up to about sixty-seven million iterations for any in-flight transmit to drain and, on success, installs the early write handler; if the channel stays busy it reports absence of device.

Character output to the debug channel spins while transmit-busy is signalled and then emits one byte; block output repeats this per byte and reports full count, while block input drains at most the requested bytes while receive-ready is signalled and reports how many were taken.

Channel presence is probed by emitting a line break and waiting about a tenth of a second for transmit to become idle; success latches a sticky availability flag that lets non-zero cores short-circuit later checks when SMP serialization is enabled.
A dedicated spin lock guards the input and output FIFOs and is always taken with interrupt state saved around FIFO movement and direct channel access in work handlers and serialized wrappers.

When SMP serialization is disabled both directions touch the channel directly; when enabled only core zero with an empty FIFO touches it directly, otherwise output is appended to the output FIFO and input is drained from the input FIFO with a work item scheduled on core zero to move data.

Both console and device initialization first probe the channel and abort with nodev status when absent; device setup disables CPU hotplug under SMP serialization and then allocates hypervisor console zero with a one-hundred-twenty-eight byte buffer, while console setup instantiates the same operations.
The console interrupt handler polls the associated hypervisor console and kicks the service thread when a repoll is requested, always reporting the interrupt as handled.

IRQ notifier helpers attach the console interrupt handler with the instance flags and record success, detach by freeing and clearing the recorded flag, and implement hangup as detach; a zero IRQ number means no request is made.

The wire message begins with one-byte version and type fields, a two-byte payload length, then a variable payload; total on-wire size is header offset plus payload length and the structure is packed without padding.
Protocol version is two; type codes are one for error, two for environment, four for termios, eight for window size and sixteen for data; maximum payload is the largest unsigned sixteen-bit value.

Per-line state holds a console reference, an eight-byte service name, a console flag, connection and tty state enums, a path pointer, a spin lock, a page-sized send buffer with length, a delayed work item with wait queue, outgoing and incoming message lists, a device pointer and path info bytes.
Each queued message wrapper links into a list, stores transport message metadata, tracks a read offset into the payload and points at the wire message buffer.

Connection moves among disconnected, connected and severed values while the tty moves between closed and opened; cleanup forces disconnected plus closed and clears buffered length, and several paths deliberately keep an established connection across tty hangup.

Send buffer capacity is one page and must stay below the maximum payload; queueing delays transmission by one twenty-fifth of a second, synchronous flush waits up to one tenth of a second, console index is zero and the default line count is one.

Inbound retrieval returns idle when disconnected or when no messages wait and pipe error when severed; it receives the head message once, discards on transport error or version and length mismatch, copies data with offset tracking and more-data signalling, applies window-size updates under console lock and ignores control types.

Outbound queueing silently counts dropped bytes while disconnected, fails with pipe error when severed, otherwise appends up to free send-buffer space and schedules delayed transmission when connected; sending wraps buffered bytes into one data message, queues it, attempts transport send and on failure drops it while always clearing the staging length.

The per-line spin lock protects state flags, staging length and both queues and is taken in process and bottom-half forms around queue manipulation; path teardown is always performed outside the lock because of ordering against the transport table lock.

Local hangup flushes synchronously then marks the tty closed and only cleans up when already severed so an established path survives; remote sever marks severed and either cleans up when closed or for consoles or kicks the service thread; lowering modem signals flushes and forces disconnected with outside-lock teardown; deletion flushes, destroys both queues and resets length.

Connection filtering allows up to five hundred eight-byte entries with star as wildcard for prefix matching and accepts all when no filter is configured; the line table size derives from the tty adapter count and the buffer pool minimum derives from page size over wrapper size quartered.

Presence probing unconditionally emits a newline and spins with relaxed waiting, and enabling SMP serialization disables CPU hotplug so core zero cannot go offline after the online check; work scheduling is skipped when core zero is offline which can leave queued bytes pending.

Receive keeps the head descriptor queued when payload allocation fails and reports memory shortage for later retry, while synchronous flush cancels delayed work, forces one send and then sleeps briefly for the outgoing queue to drain which may still be non-empty on timeout.
A registered transport handler maps pending, severed, completion and incoming-message events to the line state machine callbacks.

Line lookup bounds-checks the index against the configured device count and returns null when out of range; message wrappers come from a dedicated pool with zeroed metadata and an optional DMA-capable payload preset to current version and data type, and list destruction unlinks and frees each entry.
Diagnostic output from this driver carries a fixed module prefix.
